notes: NNS-core is the portable C++ extraction of the R NNS src layer. The R repo remains authoritative. r_commit/r_src_tree_hash identify the R src tree the core was ported from (original_src/ holds the corresponding R files byte for byte); core_commit is the last NNS-core commit that ported numerics from it. `r_bug_fixes` lists R bugs that NNS-core fixes ahead of R: there the core intentionally differs from this r_commit, and the fidelity suite tags the affected cases with `r_fix`.

r_bug_fixes.summary: vectorised (>32 targets) LPM/UPM prefix backend cancels catastrophically for degree >= 3; replaced by a cancellation-free sorted-anchor recurrence
discrete NNS.mode keyed on int (UB beyond the int range, 3e9 -> -2147483648)
gravity/mode histogram bin count unbounded and computed as int; long empty runs are now shortened (bit-identical results, O(n) bins)
generate.vectors lag > n out-of-bounds read; generate.lin.vectors(x, 0) division by zero
negative / NaN degrees silently accepted; now rejected
the 1-D duplicated-coordinate fast path compared raw |x - t| instead of the range-normalised distances, so neighbours and ties (and the prediction) depended on the other queries in the batch
native M.reg distances multiplied by a precomputed 1/range, which rounds differently from the R reference's division and can flip exact nearest-neighbour ties (50 vs 100)
degree-0 Co.UPM_nD/DPM_nD and the bivariate copula's discordant count treated ties inconsistently, so CLPM + CUPM + DPM did not partition the sample
native noise.reduction = "mode" reducer took the most frequent exact value instead of NNS.mode, unlike R's own pure-R path
copula_signed returned +1 for fully discordant cells, so NNS.dep(x, -x) reported Correlation +1
copula_signed compared the concordant share count * (1/n) with 1, false for many n (49 * (1/49) != 1)
NNS.mode ordered equally high peaks with std::sort, so the kept peaks and the single mode depended on the standard library; now bin order breaks ties and the single mode averages the highest peaks
the pairwise SD test walked both samples with the first sample's length, so .uni results for samples of unequal length were wrong
the pairwise SD test reported dominance in both directions when the curves coincide (also continuous FSD ratios equal at every knot)
continuous FSD mapped the 0/0 ratio at a point mass to 0 instead of the CDF value, as LPM.ratio does
TSD and continuous FSD were checked only at the sample points, missing curve crossings between them
SD verdicts compared curves exactly, so rounding noise decided them; now a 64 * DBL_EPSILON relative tie tolerance with compensated prefix sums
